b: Question: What’s the best piece of gear you acquired this year?
Josh Rouse, singer, songwriter, and guitarist
Rouse’s new album, Museums and Women, is out now on New West Records.

A: A handmade little amp called the Henriksen Bud SIX out of Colorado. I like Hendrick’s Gin as well, so maybe there’s something there. I was in London for a solo acoustic show and wasn’t sure my pickup was working, so I wandered into a little boutique guitar shop near my hotel and asked if I could plug in. They handed me a cable and set me up with a 10-inch Henriksen, which I’d never heard of, and it sounded incredible. They told me all the jazz cats in London were using the Bud SIX, this tiny amp you can basically strap over your shoulder. It weighs about 13 pounds, puts out 120 clean watts through a 6-inch speaker, and has an incredible tone. I bought one when I got home. Best piece of gear I’ve found in years.

Obsession: The work of Finnish filmmaker Aki Kaurismäki. My favorites are Le Havre and La Vie de Bohème. His films have a certain look and feel that inspires me to write songs or just pick up a guitar and play. Everything is very sparse and basic, but there’s such great taste in the color, set design, and framing. They don’t tell you how to feel so much as invite you into a mood, which is usually where I like songs to begin.

A: The Shure GLXD16+ Digital Wireless Guitar Pedal System. Two weeks ago I played my biggest show ever and was counting on it to perform well, and it was flawless. I love the ease of setup—it’s literally just power on and play. You just turn the wireless from your guitar on, it automatically searches for the best channel and connects. The built-in tuner is a nice touch, and the warranty coverage for these units are great.

Obsession: Going to farms near me in the Midwest and playing and singing to the animals, specifically the cows. Music is the bridge to so many walks of life, and music to cows is no different than to humans—their responses are genuinely curious, and they always run over to see what’s going on! Another one is the Epiphone Inspired by Gibson Pre-War SJ-200 Sunburst. I snagged them at Dave’s Guitar Shop in Wisconsin, and love them so much I have two.

A: I recently bought Pony, a Fender Player II Mustang Bass PJ in aquatone, which I was delighted to add to my fleet of teal and blue-toned guitars. I direct a nonprofit youth rock band program, and one of the bands currently lacks a bass player. I’m the one to fill in until we can find a permanent bassist for the kids. I'm primarily a vocalist and guitar player, and with small hands, a short-scale bass was a necessity. I'm really enjoying my new skills on it. I just turned 40, and I’m vowing to never stop learning new things... even if the teenagers are better at it than me!

Obsession: I collect rocks and sand from everywhere I visit. Whether I’m on vacation or just taking a walk in the park, I usually come home with a pocketful of little pieces of nature. I just got my first microscope, and I’m completely entranced by sand from different places up close. I can take pictures through the lens, so I’m guessing my walls will soon be covered in framed close-ups of sand. Life gets better when you start noticing all the small, sacred things around you. They’re everywhere.
